archetypes.name: porting-parity
archetypes.rationale: The diff ports two Bash helpers to Python; exact behavioral parity is critical because callers depend on identical regex semantics, block-splitting, and security-classification logic.
archetypes.prompt_body: Examine whether python/oos.py faithfully replicates the retired Bash behavior in skills/shared/scripts/oos-serialize.sh and normalize-oos-block-header.sh. Focus on: (1) the block-splitting in _iter_finding_blocks — does it lose trailing content or produce extra blank lines that the retired awk did not? (2) the _HEADER_TOKEN_RE pattern uses re.sub with count=1 and an anchored ^ — verify the substitution is exactly equivalent to the awk sub() on NR==1. (3) The double-write pattern in oos_serialize (truncate to empty first, then write full output) — confirm this preserves the fail-closed guarantee: if _classify_security raises, the file remains empty rather than holding partial blocks. (4) The _security_classifier() indirection returns is_security_tagged unconditionally — verify there are no paths where a monkeypatch-injected classifier fails to propagate through this indirection. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: caller-integration
archetypes.rationale: Three runtime callers now invoke `python3 ... cli.py oos ...` instead of the retired shell scripts; stdout routing, exit-code handling, and Python availability must match expectations exactly.
archetypes.prompt_body: Review the three caller cutover sites: skills/review/scripts/emit-tally.sh, skills/review/scripts/tally-code-votes.sh, and skills/review-and-fix/scripts/review-and-fix.sh. For tally-code-votes.sh the normalize-header call captures stdout into a file via redirection — confirm that python/oos.py oos_normalize_header_main writes only the normalized block to stdout with no debug output or extra newlines that would corrupt the captured file. For emit-tally.sh the serialize call uses >>/dev/null, discarding stdout KEY=VALUE pairs — verify this is intentional and no caller reads those keys. For review-and-fix.sh the normalize-header call appends stdout to $skipped_file — check that any failure (non-zero exit from python3) is handled or at least does not silently produce a truncated or empty append. Also check whether `python3` is assumed on PATH in all three callers and whether there is any guard or fallback if it is absent, matching the behavior of the retired shell scripts. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.
